data.title: Green Beans with Shallots and Lemon
ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
10 g salt, for the boiling water
1/8 tsp fine salt, for finishing, optional after tasting
2 tbsp water, for warming the beans if needed
data.description: Green beans cooked until pleasantly tender, then warmed with softened shallots and finished with measured lemon. Honey is a small optional accent.

learning.focus: Use tenderness to finish green vegetables and add acid near service
learning.outcome: Hot beans that bend and bite cleanly, with softened shallots and a light lemon coating rather than hard centers or a sweet puddle.
before: The default is cook-and-serve: drain the boiled beans and finish them directly in the shallot pan. An ice bath is useful when preparing beans ahead, not required before every immediate serving.
Bean thickness and age matter. Slender haricots verts may soften sooner than thick mature beans; taste a cooled piece instead of insisting on an exact three-minute blanch.
A full four-portion finish fits a 12-inch skillet. Larger amounts need separate batches or another skillet, not a tightly packed mound.

checkpoints.cue: A bean bends and can be bitten through with a little resistance, without a fibrous raw center.
checkpoints.why: Bright color alone does not indicate tenderness. The brief pan finish mainly warms and coats the beans.

checkpoints.cue: Shallots are soft and translucent with no dark bitter edges.
checkpoints.why: A short gentle saute develops their sweetness; honey and lemon do not instantly caramelize undercooked shallots.

checkpoints.cue: The hot beans have a light coating, and lemon is noticeable without pooling in the pan.
checkpoints.why: Acid can dull chlorophyll during extended heating. Finishing off heat limits that exposure; cooling does not permanently lock in green color.

troubleshooting.problem: Beans are bright green but tough
troubleshooting.cause: Their size or age needed more cooking than the timer allowed.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep boiling and check a piece every minute. Do not drain simply because the color looks ready.

troubleshooting.cause: Heat is too high for the small dice.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the heat and add a little of the listed finishing water to help soften them. Discard blackened pieces rather than hiding bitterness with honey.

troubleshooting.problem: Sauce tastes too sweet or acidic
troubleshooting.cause: A full spoonful of honey or an entire juicy lemon overwhelmed this amount of beans.
troubleshooting.fix: Start with the defined small amounts and taste before the optional additions. If already over-seasoned, additional plain cooked beans can dilute it; cooking longer will not remove the sugar.

substitutions.ingredient: 1 tbsp unsalted butter and optional honey
substitutions.alternative: 1 tbsp olive oil and omit honey
substitutions.effect: Makes the default ingredients vegan, with less buttery flavor and no added sweetness.

substitutions.alternative: 450 g plain frozen green beans
substitutions.effect: Follow the package's cooking directions, drain and finish in the shallot pan. They are already blanched and often softer; do not apply the fresh-bean timing unchanged.

learning.timing: Allow about thirty-five minutes including trimming, shallot preparation, bringing the water to a boil, three to six minutes bean cooking and the skillet finish. Soften shallots while the water heats. Prepared-ahead beans need about fifteen minutes for shallots and reheating, with the earlier preparation counted separately.
learning.storage: For preparation a day ahead, cool cooked beans promptly in ice water until cold, drain thoroughly and refrigerate covered at 40°F / 4°C or below. Keep lemon and shallot finishing for service. Reheat refrigerated cooked beans to 165°F / 74°C before the lemon finish. Refrigerate finished leftovers within two hours, or one hour above 90°F / 32°C, and use within three to four days; texture and color soften on reheating.

sources.title: Exploratorium — Heat, acid and green vegetable pigments
University of Minnesota Extension — Cooling blanched vegetables
FoodSafety.gov — Cooling, storage and reheating

body:
## Chef's Note

Cook the beans to a texture you enjoy, then dress them. Shallots bring a gentle sweetness; a teaspoon of optional honey is enough to soften the lemon edge without turning this into candied vegetables. Lemon goes in at the end because prolonged heating with acid dulls green color. An ice bath slows further cooking when holding beans ahead, but does not permanently protect their color or texture.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the vegetables and water:** Trim the beans, rinse and drain. Dice the shallots, zest the lemon and measure its juice. Bring two liters of water with ten grams salt to a boil in a 4-quart pot. Begin the shallots in step three while the water heats if you can watch both pans.
2. **Cook to tenderness:** Add beans and return to a gentle boil. Begin tasting after three minutes; many beans need four to six minutes, and very thick ones can need longer. A cooled piece should bite cleanly with a little resistance. Drain thoroughly. For immediate serving, keep them warm and move straight to the skillet finish; do not chill them first.
3. **Soften shallots:** Melt butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat. Add shallots and cook five to seven minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent. Lower heat if they begin browning sharply. Use a small splash from the listed finishing water if needed to help them soften.
4. **Warm and coat:** Add the drained beans and optional teaspoon of honey. Toss gently over medium heat for two to three minutes until hot and lightly coated. If the pan is dry, add a little of the remaining finishing water. For refrigerated prepared-ahead beans, allow about four to six minutes, cover briefly with the water as needed, and check they reach 165°F / 74°C before proceeding; then uncover so excess water evaporates.
5. **Finish off heat:** Remove from heat. Add lemon zest, the first tablespoon of juice and pepper. Toss, taste a bean and add the optional finishing salt or extra teaspoon of juice only if needed. Divide among four plates and serve promptly.

## Preparing ahead

After step two, chill beans in a bowl of ice water until cold, then drain thoroughly and refrigerate as described above. This makes the final shallot-and-bean step easier to coordinate with a roast, at the cost of another heating cycle. Use fresh lemon at service. Do not leave a bowl of cooked beans at room temperature for the afternoon.

data.title: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
ingredients: 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, divided
3 to 4 tbsp Thai green curry paste, according to its strength
1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed when frying the paste
1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little hot water only if needed to loosen
250 g Japanese or Chinese eggplant, trimmed, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/2 inch thick
75 g canned bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
4 makrut lime leaves, torn into large pieces
1 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually only as needed
1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, plus a little more only if needed
data.description: Chicken, eggplant, pepper, and bamboo shoots in a fluid green-curry coconut sauce, finished with Thai basil.

learning.focus: Develop the paste, then preserve a fluid curry sauce
learning.outcome: Tender chicken and yielding eggplant in a fragrant, pourable coconut curry with fresh basil aroma.
before: Paste brands vary in heat, salt and concentration. Start at the lower end with an unfamiliar paste; do not assume every tablespoon has equal strength.
Full-fat coconut milk may stay emulsified because of its processing or stabilizers. A visible oil split is useful when it happens, but not a mandatory success signal.

checkpoints.cue: Paste smells fragrant and has cooked without scorching, whether or not a little oil separates.
checkpoints.why: Aromatic development depends on cooking the paste. Continuing until every brand visibly splits can burn a paste that is already ready.

checkpoints.cue: The thickest chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and eggplant centers yield easily.
checkpoints.why: A safe chicken endpoint and a tender vegetable center need separate checks; surface color does not establish either.

checkpoints.cue: The curry pours around the solids, and the seasoning is savory without being excessively salty.
checkpoints.why: Green curry has more liquid than panang. Reducing it to a sticky coating concentrates salt and changes the dish.

troubleshooting.cause: The milk remains emulsified under these cooking conditions.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the measured oil if the paste needs it and move on once fragrant. Do not keep reducing a dry paste just to see separated oil.

troubleshooting.problem: Chicken is ready but eggplant is still firm
troubleshooting.cause: The eggplant pieces were thick or partly above the liquid.
troubleshooting.fix: Lift cooked chicken out briefly and simmer the eggplant until tender, then return chicken to warm through.

troubleshooting.problem: Curry is too thick or strongly seasoned
troubleshooting.cause: It reduced too far or the paste was especially concentrated.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a little hot water to restore a fluid sauce. Next time use less paste or fish sauce; sugar alone does not undo excessive salt or heat.

substitutions.alternative: 1/2 tsp finely grated ordinary lime zest at the finish
substitutions.effect: Provides a different citrus aroma and cannot duplicate the leaves. Do not add a tablespoon of zest or lime juice as an equivalent.

substitutions.alternative: 680 g chicken breast cut into 1-inch pieces
substitutions.effect: Simmer vegetables first until almost tender, then add breast and cook only until 165°F / 74°C; it dries more readily than thigh meat.

substitutions.alternative: Products labeled gluten-free
substitutions.effect: Check both packages and the stock. The recipe is not automatically gluten-free just because rice is served alongside.

learning.timing: About 45 minutes includes preparation, coconut/paste cooking, heating, and the chicken/vegetable simmer. Rice is a separate recipe.
learning.storage: Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C), at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days; reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat gently; eggplant softens further and basil darkens. Stir separated coconut fat back in if preferred.

body:
## Chef's Note

Chicken, Asian eggplant, red pepper and bamboo shoots sit in a fragrant coconut sauce with Thai basil. Leave enough sauce to spoon around the solids and over rice. Cook the paste until fragrant without scorching it; some canned coconut milks will not visibly split into oil.

## Directions

1. **Prepare ingredients:** Cut vegetables and pick basil before handling raw chicken, then clean the board and tools. Measure 120 ml of the coconut milk for the paste; use the thick top portion if it has separated, or stir the can and measure if uniform. Reserve the rest.
2. **Cook coconut and paste:** In a wide saucepan, simmer the 120 ml coconut milk over medium heat about 3–5 minutes until thickened, stirring. Add green curry paste and cook about 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. If it sticks and has not released oil, add the measured tablespoon of neutral oil; a small splash of the reserved coconut milk can also loosen the pan. Do not require darkening or oil pooling before continuing.
3. **Start chicken:** Stir in chicken, remaining coconut milk, stock and torn lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer, separating the chicken pieces, and cook about 5 minutes. Do not taste the curry while chicken is still undercooked.
4. **Cook vegetables and check:** Add eggplant, pepper and bamboo shoots. Simmer gently about 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally so pieces are exposed to the hot liquid, until eggplant is tender and several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Extend as needed; if chicken finishes well before eggplant, follow troubleshooting.
5. **Season and finish:** Add the sugar and start with about 1 tsp fish sauce. Taste and add more fish sauce only as needed; some pastes need very little. If too thick, add a small splash of hot water. Remove the large lime-leaf pieces, turn off heat, and fold in basil. Serve four main portions with separately prepared plain rice.

data.title: Green Smoothie
ingredients: 3/4 cup Almond Milk (or milk of choice)

body:
## Chef's Note

Frozen mango and fresh avocado blend together into a thick, creamy smoothie that masks spinach's leafy texture. The avocado provides healthy fats and silkiness, while oats add complex carbohydrates for sustained energy. Vanilla extract creates milkshake-like aroma that makes this green smoothie appealing to young palates.

## Directions

1.  **The Stack:** In a high-speed blender, add ingredients in this exact order: milk, oats, spinach, banana, avocado, and finally the frozen mango. Placing the greens at the bottom ensures they are completely pulverized first.
2.  **Process:** Blend on low, then quickly increase to high speed. Process for 60 seconds until the mixture is a vibrant, uniform green with no visible leaf flecks.
3.  **Adjust:** If the smoothie is too thick, add a splash more milk. If you need more "High Note" sweetness, add 1 tsp of maple syrup and pulse again.
4.  **Serve:** Serve immediately in a chilled glass with a wide straw.

data.title: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
ingredients: 1 (28 oz) can whole peeled San Marzano-style tomatoes, with their juices
1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the soup
4 slices sourdough or brioche, of similar size and moderate thickness
4 thin slices sharp Cheddar or Gruyère, sized to fit the bread
2 tbsp mayonnaise, for the outside of the bread
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
data.description: A quick creamy tomato soup with golden grilled-cheese sandwiches filled with avocado.

learning.focus: Finish the soup before gently toasting sandwiches so cheese melts before bread burns
learning.outcome: Hot smooth tomato soup with golden bread, melted cheese and creamy avocado inside the sandwiches.
before: This recipe includes its own cream-based soup and sandwiches. Use bread slices of similar size and not excessively thick; cheese slices should cover them without hanging far beyond the edges.

An immersion blender avoids transferring soup: remove the pot from heat, keep the blade guard submerged while running and stop before lifting it out. For a countertop blender, check that the jar and lid are approved for warm or hot liquids, cool to the manufacturer’s allowed temperature, obey its fill limit and venting instructions, and start low. Never blend hot soup in a sealed personal cup.

Use a 3-quart saucepan and a skillet large enough for the sandwiches with room to turn. For more diners use another skillet or cook in rounds; keep the soup gently hot while the sandwiches finish. Ingredient scaling does not increase a skillet’s surface area.

checkpoints.cue: Onion is soft and garlic fragrant without dark burned pieces.
checkpoints.why: Garlic needs less cooking than onion and goes in later.

checkpoints.cue: Soup is smooth and hot, with cream blended in rather than boiling hard.
checkpoints.why: Finish the soup first so sandwich melting receives your attention.

checkpoints.cue: Bread is golden on both sides and cheese is melted through the center.
checkpoints.why: Crust color can run ahead of cheese melting; moderate heat is more useful than pressing hard.

troubleshooting.problem: Bread browns but cheese stays firm
troubleshooting.cause: Heat is too high, bread too thick or cheese slices too thick.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower heat and cover the skillet briefly to help warm the filling, then uncover to restore the crust. Do not press the filling out of the sandwich.

troubleshooting.cause: The mayonnaise layer is thick for the chosen bread.
troubleshooting.fix: Spread a thin even film; the measured amount is an allowance, not a requirement to leave thick white patches.

troubleshooting.cause: Tomato acidity varies.
troubleshooting.fix: Taste with the sandwich first; its cheese and bread change the balance. Avoid adding unlisted sugar automatically. Next time choose canned tomatoes whose flavor you prefer.

substitutions.alternative: The same volume of vegetable broth
substitutions.effect: Makes the soup meat-free; for a vegetarian meal also choose cheese made with suitable rennet.

substitutions.alternative: The listed Gruyère option in similarly thin slices
substitutions.effect: A nuttier flavor and different melt; judge the center rather than relying only on the timer.

learning.timing: Allow about 55 minutes: fifteen minutes preparing, about eight minutes onion softening plus garlic, heating and a fifteen-minute soup simmer, then blending/cream and eight-to-twelve minutes for sandwiches. Assemble sandwiches while soup simmers, but finish blending before cooking them. More sandwich rounds add time.
learning.storage: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Do not leave a deep stockpot cooling on the counter until cold. Plan to use the next day for quality. Reheat the portion needed, stirring, to 165°F / 74°C throughout; add a little water only if it has thickened too much. Keep sandwiches separate from soup and refrigerate them promptly too. Their bread and avocado lose texture; next-day reheating is a compromise, not a fresh grilled-cheese result.

body:
## Chef's Note

Make the soup first and keep it gently hot while the sandwiches cook. A thin mayonnaise layer helps the bread brown evenly, but heat control still matters: lower the heat if the crust darkens before the cheese melts. Avocado belongs inside, where it contrasts with the crisp exterior.

## Directions

1. **Soften aromatics:** Melt the measured butter in a saucepan over medium-low. Cook onion about **6–8 minutes** until soft, then add garlic for **30–45 seconds** until fragrant.
2. **Simmer soup:** Add all listed tomatoes and juices, broth and dried basil. Break up tomatoes with a spoon, bring to a gentle simmer and cook about **15 minutes**, stirring, until soft. Prepare sandwich ingredients while it simmers.
3. **Blend and add cream:** Remove from heat and let active bubbling stop. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping its guard submerged and stopping before lifting it. Alternatively, cool to your countertop blender’s permitted temperature and blend in as many small batches as its hot-liquid fill limit requires, with the lid and steam vent arranged exactly as its instructions specify. Start low; do not use a sealed personal cup for hot soup. Stir in cream and season with salt and pepper. Warm gently and keep hot at **140°F / 60°C or above** for the brief sandwich cooking period, without a hard boil.
4. **Assemble sandwiches:** Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on one face of each bread slice, using only what is needed from the measured allowance. Place **half the bread slices**, mayonnaise-side down, in a cool skillet. Divide all the cheese and avocado evenly over these bases. Top with the remaining bread, mayonnaise-side up.
5. **Toast gently:** Set over medium-low to medium heat. Cook about **4–6 minutes per side**, turning carefully, until golden and cheese has melted in the center. Lower heat if bread colors too quickly; cover briefly if the center needs help warming, then uncover. Use additional rounds if the skillet is crowded.
6. **Serve together:** Cut sandwiches as desired and divide the soup among the intended portions. Serve immediately for dipping; do not leave the sandwiches sitting in the soup.

data.title: Chicken with Herbed Corn Salsa
ingredients: 1/4 cup Fresh Lemon Juice (The Finishing Touch)

body:
## Chef's Note

This Mexican-inspired grilled chicken showcases summer corn charred directly on the grill until the kernels develop smoky, caramelized spots. The herb salsa combines fresh basil and mint with lemon and Parmesan, creating a bright, aromatic topping. The lemon's acidity cuts through the rich fat of chicken thighs.

## Directions

1.  **The Chicken:** Preheat grill to medium-high. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Grill, skin-side down first, for 15-20 minutes total, turning once, until the skin is crispy and internal temp reaches 165°F.
2.  **The Corn:** Place corn ears directly on the grill. Cook for 10 minutes, rotating occasionally, until charred in spots.
3.  **The Salsa:** While grilling, place basil, mint, Parmesan, and garlic in a food processor. Pulse until finely chopped. Drizzle in the lemon juice and olive oil and pulse once more until a chunky emulsion forms.
4.  **Combine:** Shear the charred kernels off the cobs. In a small bowl, toss the kernels with the herb sauce.
5.  **Serve:** Place grilled chicken on a platter and top generously with the herbed corn salsa. Serve immediately.

data.title: Pork and Peaches
ingredients: 2 lbs Boneless Pork Butt (or Shoulder), butterflied

body:
## Chef's Note

Pounding pork butt to uniform 3/4-inch thickness breaks down tough connective tissue and ensures it sears at the same rate as the fruit. Grilling peaches in butter until soft and slightly charred caramelizes their sugars while developing acidity that cuts through the rich, rosemary-crusted pork. This classic American summer pairing showcases stone fruit at peak season.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Place butterflied pork on a board. Use a meat mallet to pound to an even 3/4-inch thickness. Season aggressively with salt and pepper.
2.  **The Paste:** In a small bowl, whisk garlic, rosemary, and 6 tbsp of the olive oil into a thick paste. Rub the paste over both sides of the pork.
3.  **The Sear:** Heat a large cast-iron griddle or grill to high. Brush with remaining oil. Place pork on the heat and sear **without moving** for 8-10 minutes until a deep crust forms.
4.  **The Fruit:** While pork sears, place the peach halves (cut-side down) around the meat. Dot the fruit with the diced butter. Grill for 5 minutes until soft and charred. Transfer peaches to a platter.
5.  **Flip:** Turn the pork over and cook for another 5-7 minutes until the internal temp reaches 145°F (for a perfect blush pink).
6.  **Rest:** Remove meat to a carving board and **rest for 5 minutes** (mandatory for structure).
7.  **Serve:** Slice the pork and serve immediately with the buttery, charred peaches and any pan juices.

data.title: Banh Mi
ingredients: 1.5 lbs Pork Tenderloin or Butt, thinly sliced
2 stalks Lemongrass, finely minced (white parts only)
Mayonnaise and liquid seasoning (or soy sauce)

body:
## Chef's Note

Banh mi sandwiches are Vietnamese street food defined by contrast: grilled pork against pickled vegetables, cilantro, and creamy mayo on crusty bread. The marinade is garlic, fish sauce, and brown sugar - a workhorse base that caramelizes on the grill. The pickled vegetables are non-negotiable: they're the cooling, cutting element that makes the sandwich balanced.

## Directions

1.  **Marinate:** Whisk fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic, and lemongrass. Toss with the pork. Let marinate for at least 2 hours (ideally overnight).
2.  **Pickles:** Prepare your [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon) while the pork marinates: allow about 20 minutes for cutting and packing, then at least 1 hour in the refrigerator before serving. Keep them refrigerated until assembly.
3.  **Grill:** Thread pork onto skewers or use a grill basket. Wipe off excess marinade and grill over medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and just cooked through.
4.  **Assemble:** Split the baguettes. Spread a generous layer of mayo. Drizzle with a few drops of liquid seasoning or soy sauce.
5.  **Fill:** Layer the grilled pork, cucumber spears, [Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon), and fresh cilantro. Top with jalapeños for heat.

data.title: Grilled Zucchini with Mint and Lemon
ingredients: 680 g small-to-medium zucchini, trimmed and sliced lengthwise into 3/8-inch planks
2 tbsp olive oil, divided between cooking and finishing
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus 1 tsp more only if needed
data.description: Even zucchini planks cooked until tender with browned patches, then finished with measured lemon, mint and olive oil.

learning.focus: Match heat and plank thickness so the center softens before the outside burns
learning.outcome: Warm zucchini with browned patches, a tender center and enough structure to lift intact, finished with fresh mint and lemon.
before: Choose smaller zucchini with firm flesh and modest seed cavities. Slice to an even thickness and dry the surfaces before oiling.
A stovetop grill pan may need three rounds for 680 g. The default thirty-five-minute allowance includes pan heating and repeated batches; a large outdoor grill may be faster.

checkpoints.cue: Planks lift with tongs and bend slightly; a fork meets only light resistance in the center.
checkpoints.why: Dark grill lines show surface contact, not complete cooking. Thickness and heat determine whether the interior is tender before the outside burns.

checkpoints.cue: Lemon lightly coats the warm planks and mint is added after the cooking heat.
checkpoints.why: A late finish retains more fresh herb aroma; it does not mean all flavor is instantly destroyed by any heat.

troubleshooting.problem: Black lines but a hard center
troubleshooting.cause: Heat was too strong for the thickness or planks were uneven.
troubleshooting.fix: Move to gentler heat and cook longer, turning as needed. Avoid chasing darker marks. Cut the next batch evenly.

troubleshooting.cause: It cooked too long, used large seedy squash or was piled under a tight cover.
troubleshooting.fix: Spread in a single layer and spoon off excess liquid. Lost firmness cannot be restored; use the soft pieces in a sandwich or chopped salad.

substitutions.alternative: 2 tbsp torn basil
substitutions.effect: A sweeter herbal finish without mint’s cooling character; add after cooking in the same way.

substitutions.alternative: A heavy skillet
substitutions.effect: Use the same oil allocation and batches. Broad browning replaces grill stripes; judge the center, not a pictured pattern.

learning.timing: About thirty-five minutes allows ten minutes preparation and heating plus up to three 6–8-minute grill-pan rounds. A larger outdoor grill that holds all planks can reduce batch time. A short serving hold is optional, not a mandatory flavor-development wait.
learning.storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C), at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within three days. Eat properly chilled leftovers cold, or reheat the portion being served to 165°F / 74°C; reheating softens the planks and dulls the fresh herb finish.

sources.title: Jeanine Donofrio — Grilled zucchini texture and timing cues
FoodSafety.gov — Clean, separate, cook, chill
USDA FSIS — Leftovers and food safety

body:
## Chef's Note

Zucchini needs enough heat to brown, but an extremely hot grill can blacken the contact lines before a thick center softens. Even planks and a fork check make the method repeatable. Finish with lemon and mint after cooking, then serve with their aroma still fresh.

## Directions

1. **Heat and slice:** Preheat a clean grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Trim zucchini and slice into even 3/8-inch lengthwise planks. Pat the surfaces dry. For a stovetop pan, plan several uncrowded rounds.
2. **Oil and season:** Reserve 1/2 tbsp of the oil for finishing. Brush the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp over both sides of all the planks and distribute the measured salt and pepper. Oil coats the vegetables; do not add another unmeasured pour to the pan.
3. **Cook in batches:** Lay planks across the grill bars with space, using tongs. Cook about 3–4 minutes per side, turning once they release and have browned patches. Reduce heat if they blacken quickly. Check a thick center with a fork: it should be tender with light resistance, and the plank should lift intact. Transfer to a broad platter and repeat with remaining planks; do not pile and tightly cover the finished ones.
4. **Dress and taste:** Drizzle the cooked zucchini with the reserved 1/2 tbsp oil and initial tablespoon of lemon juice. Add mint and zest, then turn gently. Taste before adding any of the optional extra teaspoon of lemon.
5. **Serve:** Divide into four sides and serve warm, or after a brief hold while the main finishes. The planks will soften somewhat as they stand; this is not a promise that holding always improves them.

data.title: Guacamole
data.source: Adapted from Alton Brown's Guacamole
ingredients: 2 Roma tomatoes, cored, seeded and finely diced
data.description: Chunky avocado with tomato, red onion, garlic, cumin and a warm cayenne kick. Add lime and salt in stages, then taste with the food it will accompany.

learning.focus: Balance a chunky avocado mash without making it watery
learning.outcome: Creamy avocado holds the diced vegetables, with some soft chunks, a noticeable spice warmth and lime that brightens without pooling in the bowl.
before: Avocados should yield gently to palm pressure and mash readily. Three fruits do not give a fixed flesh weight or finished volume; larger fruit may need more of the reserved seasoning.
Drain loose juice from the diced tomatoes. Jalapeño and cayenne together make a spicy dip; omit both for a mild version.

checkpoints.cue: The mash is mostly creamy with small soft avocado chunks remaining.
checkpoints.why: Hand mashing gives texture without crushing every vegetable into a wet paste.

checkpoints.cue: Tomato and onion are evenly distributed and no watery ring collects around the mash.
checkpoints.why: Removing loose tomato juice and staging lime keeps the avocado flavor concentrated.

checkpoints.cue: After the rest, the flavor is savory and gently tart rather than sharply sour or aggressively salty.
checkpoints.why: The finished dip and its salty accompaniments are the useful final seasoning reference.

troubleshooting.cause: Tomatoes carried loose juice or too much lime was added.
troubleshooting.fix: Fold in extra plain ripe avocado if available. Avoid adding more acid to correct it; excess liquid cannot be removed cleanly once the mash is mixed.

troubleshooting.cause: Cut avocado was exposed to air during holding.
troubleshooting.fix: For the next hold, smooth the surface, press food wrap against it and refrigerate. Lime and covering slow discoloration but do not guarantee a permanently green surface.

troubleshooting.cause: The fruit was underripe or damaged.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose different ripe fruit; extra lime, mashing or a room-temperature rest will not repair it.

substitutions.alternative: Omit both for a mild version
substitutions.effect: Keeps the tomato, garlic and cumin character without the two hot-pepper ingredients.

substitutions.alternative: The same amount of finely diced white onion
substitutions.effect: Changes the onion bite and appearance while retaining fresh diced texture.

learning.timing: About 20 minutes hands-on plus a one-hour covered refrigerator rest. The rest is included in the 80-minute total. It can also be served freshly mixed in about 20 minutes; taste the seasonings before serving either way. A larger batch takes more cutting time.
learning.storage: Keep at 40°F / 4°C or below, with food wrap pressed against the surface, and use within one day for best quality. Return to the refrigerator within 2 hours of preparation or serving, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Lime does not make this dip shelf-stable or extend those limits.

California Avocado Commission — Ripeness and reducing browning
FoodSafety.gov — Clean, separate, cook and chill

body:
## Chef's Note

Adapted from Alton Brown's guacamole, this version combines avocado with tomato, garlic, cumin and cayenne. Keep the tomatoes well drained and fold them in after mashing. Add lime and salt in stages, and cover the surface closely during a refrigerated rest to limit exposure to air.

## Directions

1. **Prepare:** Rinse produce before cutting. Dice the onion and tomatoes, removing tomato cores and loose seed pulp; drain excess tomato juice. Mince jalapeño and garlic, chop cilantro, and juice the lime.
2. **Mash:** Halve and pit the avocados and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Toss with half the lime juice. Add half the measured salt, the cumin and cayenne, then mash with a fork or potato masher until creamy with small soft chunks.
3. **Fold:** Gently fold in the onion, tomatoes, jalapeño, garlic and cilantro until distributed. Keep the vegetables in distinct pieces rather than puréeing them into the mash.
4. **Rest and season:** Smooth the surface, press food wrap against it and refrigerate for about one hour. Stir gently and taste with a tortilla or other accompaniment. Add remaining lime and salt gradually only as needed. For immediate service, skip the rest and make the same seasoning check.
5. **Serve:** Share as four generous dip portions or use smaller spoonfuls as a taco or fajita topping. Finished volume varies with avocado size. Keep covered and refrigerated until needed.

data.title: Ham & Cheese Green Bean Casserole
ingredients: 2 cans (10.75 oz) Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup

body:
## Chef's Note

This modern update transforms the classic holiday side into a main dish by adding savory ham. Par-boiling the beans in chicken broth for exactly 5 minutes before baking ensures they turn tender-crisp rather than squeaky and rubbery. Reserving half the cheddar and fried onions for the final 10 minutes creates a properly browned, crispy crust.

## Directions

1.  **Par-Boil:** In a medium pot, bring 4 cups chicken broth or water to a boil. Add green beans and cook for 5-6 minutes. Drain immediately. **Do not rinse.**
2.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Butter a 9x13 baking dish.
3.  **The Bind:** In a large bowl, whisk together the soup, half-and-half, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
4.  **Mix:** Fold in the par-boiled beans, diced ham, onion, 2 cups of the cheese, and 1/2 cup of the fried onions.
5.  **Assemble:** Pour the mixture into the baking dish.
6.  **Bake:** Bake for 30 minutes until bubbling.
7.  **The Crunch Finish:** Remove the pan. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup of cheese and the remaining 1/2 cup of fried onions over the top. Bake for an additional 10 minutes until the crust is deep golden and shatteringly crisp.
8.  **Rest:** Let sit for 5 minutes before serving to allow the sauce to set.

body:
## Chef's Note

Pre-baking the crust for 5 minutes creates a moisture barrier that prevents soggy bottom - essential for any quiche. A ratio of 5 eggs to 1/2 cup cream produces firm, sliceable custard that remains creamy rather than rubbery. Sautéing the onions in butter first develops their natural sweetness, providing contrast to salty ham.

## Directions

1.  **Blind Bake:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Pierce the bottom of the pie crust with a fork. Place on a baking sheet and bake for 5-7 minutes. Remove and set aside.
2.  **The Sauté:** In a small skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Sauté onions for 2-3 minutes until translucent. Add the ham and optional bacon; cook for 2 more minutes until slightly browned. Remove from heat.
3.  **The Custard:** In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs and half-and-half until perfectly smooth and frothy.
4.  **Assemble:** Scatter the ham mixture, spinach, and both cheeses into the pre-baked crust. Pour the egg custard slowly over the fillings.
5.  **Bake:** Reduce oven to 375°F. Bake for 25-35 minutes until the top is deep golden brown and a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
6.  **Rest:** Let the quiche rest for 10 minutes before slicing. This allows the custard to fully set.

data.title: Hamantaschen
ingredients: Apricot Jam, Poppy Seed Paste, or chocolate-hazelnut spread

body:
## Chef's Note

These triangular Jewish cookies for Purim require careful technique to prevent blowouts during baking. When folding the three sides, tuck one corner under the next flap to create a self-locking triangle. Chilling the dough until stone-cold before rolling prevents butter from melting too quickly, producing delicate, shortbread-like cookies rather than bready ones. Use exactly 1 teaspoon filling - overfilling causes leakage.

## Directions

1.  **The Emulsion:** In a stand mixer, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy (3 mins). Add the egg, vanilla, and orange zest; beat until perfectly combined.
2.  **The Mix:** Sift in the flour and salt. Mix on low speed until a crumbly dough forms. **Stop immediately.**
3.  **The Knead:** Use your hands to gently knead the crumbles into a smooth, tacky ball. If too dry, add cold water 1 tsp at a time.
4.  **The Chill:** Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for **at least 3 hours** (overnight is best).
5.  **Roll:** On a floured surface, roll dough to a uniform 1/8-inch thickness.
6.  **Cut:** Use a 3-inch round cutter to cut circles. Re-roll scraps once.
7.  **Fill & Fold:** Place 1 tsp filling in the center. Fold the three sides up to form a triangle. **The Pinwheel:** Tuck the left corner of each flap _under_ the adjacent side to lock it. Pinch the corners firmly.
8.  **Bake:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are just barely golden.
9.  **Store:** Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container to maintain the "Snap."

data.title: Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings)
ingredients: 1/2 lb Raw Shrimp, peeled, deveined, and patted dry

body:
## Chef's Note

Har gow are Cantonese shrimp dumplings with translucent, pleated wrappers - a dim sum classic and a test of a chef's skill. The dough uses wheat starch (not wheat flour) mixed with boiling water, which gelatinizes the starch instantly and creates a flexible dough that steams into a glass-like wrapper. For the filling, whip the shrimp mixture vigorously in one direction until sticky - this develops the protein structure for that characteristic bouncy texture.

## Directions

1.  **The Filling:** Finely chop the shrimp. In a large bowl, combine shrimp and all shrimp paste ingredients. Whip **vigorously in one direction** for 3 minutes until the mixture is very sticky. Fold in bamboo shoots. Chill for 30 minutes.
2.  **The Dough:** In a heatproof bowl, whisk wheat starch and cornstarch. Pour in the **boiling water** while stirring rapidly with chopsticks. Add lard/oil.
3.  **Knead:** Once cool enough to touch, knead for 2 minutes until smooth. Roll into a cylinder and divide into 18 pieces. Keep covered with a damp towel.
4.  **Shape:** Use a flat blade (lightly oiled) to flatten each dough ball into a thin 3-inch circle.
5.  **Assemble:** Place 1 tbsp filling in the center. Fold and pleat carefully (aim for 7-10 pleats) to create the signature "bonnet" shape.
6.  **Steam:** Place in a bamboo steamer on parchment. Steam over boiling water for exactly 6 minutes on high heat.
7.  **Serve:** Serve immediately with chili oil and soy sauce for the mandatory **High Note**.

1. The Filling: Finely chop the shrimp. In a large bowl, combine shrimp and all shrimp paste ingredients. Whip vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until the mixture is very sticky. Fold in bamboo shoots. Chill for 30 minutes.
2. The Dough: In a heatproof bowl, whisk wheat starch and cornstarch. Pour in the boiling water while stirring rapidly with chopsticks. Add lard/oil.
3. Knead: Once cool enough to touch, knead for 2 minutes until smooth. Roll into a cylinder and divide into 18 pieces. Keep covered with a damp towel.
4. Shape: Use a flat blade (lightly oiled) to flatten each dough ball into a thin 3-inch circle.
5. Assemble: Place 1 tbsp filling in the center. Fold and pleat carefully (aim for 7-10 pleats) to create the signature "bonnet" shape.
6. Steam: Place in a bamboo steamer on parchment. Steam over boiling water for exactly 6 minutes on high heat.
7. Serve: Serve immediately with chili oil and soy sauce for the mandatory High Note.
export.notes:
Chef's Note

Har gow are Cantonese shrimp dumplings with translucent, pleated wrappers - a dim sum classic and a test of a chef's skill. The dough uses wheat starch (not wheat flour) mixed with boiling water, which gelatinizes the starch instantly and creates a flexible dough that steams into a glass-like wrapper. For the filling, whip the shrimp mixture vigorously in one direction until sticky - this develops the protein structure for that characteristic bouncy texture.

data.title: Harvest Sheet Pan Gnocchi with Kale
ingredients: 12 oz Apple Chicken Sausage, sliced into rounds
2 cups Butternut Squash, diced into 1/2-inch cubes
1/3 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan or Nutritional Yeast

body:
## Chef's Note

Sheet-pan gnocchi is a weeknight trick that turns frozen cauliflower gnocchi into something crispy and caramelized without a pot of boiling water. The key is a single layer - crowding the pan steams everything into mush instead of roasting it. The kale should emerge dark green and shatteringly crisp, which only happens if it gets coated in oil and given space.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.
2.  **Toss:** In a massive bowl, combine gnocchi, sliced sausage, squash, and kale. Drizzle with 3 tbsp olive oil. Add rosemary, thyme, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Toss until every leaf and cube is coated.
3.  **Spread:** Spread the mixture in a **single layer** on the pan. (Crucial for the kale to crisp!)
4.  **Roast:** Bake for 24-26 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the squash is tender and the gnocchi are golden.
5.  **The Crunch:** The kale should be dark green and shatteringly crisp.
6.  **Finish:** Sprinkle with Parmesan or nutritional yeast while still piping hot. Serve immediately.

body:
## Chef's Note

Combining applesauce and Greek yogurt creates incredibly moist muffins without excessive oil - a healthier approach that maintains dense, cake-like texture. Including both grated apple (for moisture) and cubed apple (for textural crunch) ensures every bite has distinct character. Turbinado sugar sprinkled on top creates a crystalline, crunchy crust.

## Directions

1.  **Dry Mix:** Preheat oven to 425°F. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.
2.  **The Apples:** Add the grated and cubed apples to the dry mix. Toss to coat - this prevents the fruit from sinking to the bottom.
3.  **Wet Mix:** In a separate bowl, whisk oil, maple syrup, eggs, yogurt, applesauce, and vanilla until smooth and aerated.
4.  **Combine:** Pour the wet into the dry. Stir with a spatula until **just combined**. A few streaks of flour are the mandatory guard against a tough muffin.
5.  **Bake:** Divide into a lined 12-cup tin. Sprinkle the turbinado sugar over the tops. Bake at 425°F for 13-16 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
6.  **Cool:** Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes before removing.

data.title: Banana Bread
ingredients: 1/3 cup Extra-Virgin Olive Oil for depth
1/2 cup Dark Chocolate Chips or Walnuts

body:
## Chef's Note

Replacing butter with extra-virgin olive oil creates a healthier banana bread while maintaining moist, tender crumb - the oil's grassy notes amplify banana sweetness. Blending wet ingredients until perfectly emulsified before folding in flour prevents over-mixing the gluten, ensuring tender texture in every slice.

## Directions

1.  **The Emulsion:** Preheat oven to 325°F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan. In a large bowl (or blender), whisk the olive oil and honey until combined. Add the eggs, mashed bananas, and milk; whisk vigorously until smooth.
2.  **The Bloom:** Add the baking soda, vanilla, salt, and cinnamon. Whisk for 30 seconds to allow the spices to integrate into the fat.
3.  **Incorporate:** Using a large spoon, fold in the flour until **just combined**. A few tiny lumps are the mandatory guard against toughness. Fold in chocolate chips if using.
4.  **The Swirl:** Pour the batter into the prepared pan. Sprinkle a pinch of cinnamon on top and run a knife in a zig-zag pattern for a visual "High Note."
5.  **Bake:** Bake for 55-60 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
6.  **Rest:** Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. Slice only once completely cool to preserve the structural integrity.

## Chef's Note

Using the finest holes on your grater for the carrots allows them to melt into the batter, providing moisture without large, distracting chunks. Applesauce reduces oil content while maintaining dense texture. The cream cheese glaze adds welcome tanginess - dip muffin tops while cold for clean coating.

## Directions

1.  **Dry Mix:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup tin. In a medium bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
2.  **Wet Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk the shredded carrots, maple syrup, applesauce, egg, oil, and vanilla until smooth and emulsified.
3.  **Combine:** Slowly stir the flour mixture and milk into the wet ingredients until **just combined**.
4.  **Bake:** Divide batter into liners. Bake for 18-20 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
5.  **Cool:** Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool **completely** before glazing.
6.  **The Glaze:** Whisk softened cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla, and milk until smooth.
7.  **Finish:** Dip each cooled muffin top into the glaze. Sprinkle with extra shredded coconut or walnuts for a textural "High Note."

data.title: Heirloom Tomato & Pesto Galette
ingredients: 1/2 cup Sharp Cheddar or Gruyère, shredded
Flaky Sea Salt and Chili Flakes

body:
## Chef's Note

Galettes are rustic free-form tarts from France, though Italians have embraced them with summer ingredients like tomatoes and pesto. The key to avoiding a soggy crust is simple: slice your tomatoes and pat them dry with paper towels for 10 minutes to remove excess moisture. For the flakiest pastry, keep your butter cold and in pea-sized pieces - a food processor makes this easy.

## Directions

1.  **The Crust:** In a food processor, pulse flour, sugar, and salt. Add cold butter; pulse until it looks like coarse meal. Drizzle in ice water; pulse 2-3 times until dough just holds together. Form into a disk, wrap in plastic, and **chill for 30 minutes** (The Gluten Rest).
2.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3.  **The Dry Method:** Slice heirloom tomatoes and place them on paper towels. Pat the tops with more towels to absorb all surface moisture.
4.  **Assemble:** Roll dough into a 12-inch circle. Spread pesto over the center, leaving a 2-inch border. Add dollops of ricotta.
5.  **Layer:** Arrange the dry tomato slices over the ricotta.
6.  **The Fold:** Gently fold the edges of the dough over the tomatoes, pleating as you go. Brush the crust edges with olive oil and sprinkle with the shredded cheese.
7.  **Bake:** Bake for 25-30 minutes until the crust is deep golden brown and the tomatoes are concentrated.
8.  **Serve:** Garnish with flaky salt, chili flakes, and fresh herbs for the mandatory **High Note**.

## Chef's Note

Most recipes overcook pork to 160°F, producing dry meat. Sear to develop a crust, then roast until each tenderloin reaches 145°F before removing it from the oven. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing; do not rely on an assumed rise in temperature during the rest. The lemon and Dijon marinade provides acidity that cuts through rich pork fat.

## Directions

1.  **Marinate:** Combine lemon juice, zest, olive oil, garlic, herbs, mustard, and 2 tsp salt in a large sealable bag. Add pork and toss to coat. **Marinate for at least 3 hours** (ideally overnight) to allow the enzymes to tenderize the meat.
2.  **The Sear:** Preheat oven to 400°F. Remove pork from marinade (discard liquid). Season aggressively with salt and pepper. Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large oven-proof skillet over medium-high. Sear pork on all sides until deep golden brown.
3.  **Roast:** Transfer the skillet directly to the oven. Roast, beginning to check after 10 minutes, until every tenderloin reaches at least 145°F in its thickest center before removal from the oven.
4.  **The Finish:** Remove to a platter and cover tightly with foil. **Rest for 10 minutes** - this is mandatory for the juices to redistribute.
5.  **Serve:** Carve into 1/2-inch thick diagonal slices. Serve warm with the accumulated juices from the platter.

## Chef's Note

Folding whole-milk ricotta into ground chicken creates a fat-moisture barrier that keeps meatballs succulent even after searing - a technique borrowed from Italian polpette. Shaping the meat into small logs rather than balls provides more surface area for browning, developing deeper savory flavor that contrasts beautifully with the bright, herbal yogurt dressing.

## Directions

1.  **Stage 1 (Roast):** Preheat oven to 400°F. On one sheet pan, toss bone-dry chickpeas with olive oil, salt, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning. On another pan, toss sweet potato cubes with olive oil, cinnamon, and cumin. Roast both for 15-20 minutes until crispy.
2.  **The Meatballs:** In a large bowl, combine chicken, ricotta, egg, panko, shallots, greens, and lemon zest. Mix **gently** until just combined.
3.  **Shape:** Form into 12 small cylindrical logs (about 2 tbsp each).
4.  **Sear:** Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the meatballs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and the internal temp is 165°F.
5.  **The Emulsion:** In a food processor, blend the yogurt, basil, jalapeño, honey, and lemon juice until vibrant green and smooth.
6.  **Assemble:** Divide the kale among four bowls. Top with the roasted chickpeas, sweet potatoes, and meatballs.
7.  **Finish:** Drizzle generously with the dressing for the mandatory **Acid Balance**.

data.title: Homemade Chicken Stock
ingredients: 4 lbs Chicken bones (backs, necks, wings, or carcasses)
1 large Yellow Onion, unpeeled, cut into quarters

body:
## Chef's Note

A great chicken stock is all about temperature control. Never let the stock boil violently after the initial heating step; high heat emulsifies the chicken fat into the water, resulting in a greasy, cloudy broth. Instead, maintain a gentle bubble (a "smile" on the surface) to extract gelatin from the bones while keeping the stock clean and clear. Leaving the onion skins on adds a beautiful, rich amber color to the finished stock.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Place the chicken bones, onion quarters, carrots, celery, and halved garlic bulb in a large 8-to-12-quart stockpot.
2.  **Boil:** Pour in the cold water. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer.
3.  **Skim:** Skim off any gray foam or impurities that rise to the surface during the first 30 minutes of cooking. This ensures a clean flavor.
4.  **Infuse:** Add the parsley stems, thyme sprigs, bay leaf, and whole black peppercorns to the pot.
5.  **Simmer:** Simmer gently, uncovered, for 4 hours. Keep the heat low so the liquid does not boil. If the water level drops too low and exposes the bones, add a cup or two of hot water.
6.  **Strain:** Pour the stock through a colander lined with cheesecloth or a fine-mesh sieve into a large heatproof bowl. Discard the spent bones and vegetables.
7.  **Chill:** Place the bowl of stock in an ice bath to cool it rapidly. Once cool, cover and refrigerate overnight.
8.  **De-fat:** Scrape off the layer of solidified fat from the surface of the chilled stock before using or freezing.

data.title: Homemade Chili Oil
ingredients: 1 cup Neutral Oil (vegetable, canola, or peanut)
1/2 cup Red Pepper Flakes (gochugaru or crushed red pepper)
1 tbsp Sichuan Peppercorns (optional, for numbing heat)

body:
## Chef's Note

Chili oil is the secret weapon of Chinese cooking - a few spoonfuls transform dumplings, noodles, or rice into something extraordinary. The technique is simple: bloom aromatics in oil, then pour the hot oil over pepper flakes to release their color and flavor without burning. The oil temperature is critical - too hot and you'll burn the flakes (bitter), too cool and you won't extract the color (pale). Aim for 275-300°F.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce/omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1. **The Prep:** Place red pepper flakes, sesame seeds, minced garlic, ginger, salt, and sugar in a heatproof bowl. This is your flavor base.

2. **The Infuse:** In a small saucepan, combine oil, star anise, cinnamon stick, and Sichuan peppercorns if using. Heat over medium until the oil reaches 275-300°F and the spices are fragrant, about 8-10 minutes.

3. **The Pour:** Remove whole spices with a slotted spoon. Carefully pour the hot oil over the pepper flake mixture - it will sizzle dramatically. Stir immediately.

4. **The Store:** Cool promptly in a heatproof container, then refrigerate at 40°F or below within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. Use within 4 days, or freeze small portions promptly. Stir before serving. Do not store this fresh-garlic-and-ginger oil at room temperature.

Chili oil is the secret weapon of Chinese cooking - a few spoonfuls transform dumplings, noodles, or rice into something extraordinary. The technique is simple: bloom aromatics in oil, then pour the hot oil over pepper flakes to release their color and flavor without burning. The oil temperature is critical - too hot and you'll burn the flakes (bitter), too cool and you won't extract the color (pale). Aim for 275-300°F.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce/omit the spicy elements.

Mise recipe: https://jordansilton.com/mise/recipes/homemade-chili-oil/

data.title: Enchilada Sauce
ingredients: 1 tsp Apple Cider Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)

body:
## Chef's Note

This homemade enchilada sauce builds deeper flavor than store-bought versions by toasting chili powder and cumin directly in the hot oil-flour roux before adding liquid. This blooming technique releases the spices' fat-soluble aromatic oils. A splash of apple cider vinegar at the end brightens the earthy cumin and tomato paste.
For kids, serve the heat on the side or reduce/omit the spicy elements.

## Directions

1.  **The Roux:** In a medium saucepan, heat oil over medium. Whisk in the flour and all the spices (The Bloom). Cook, whisking constantly, for 1 minute until fragrant and the color deepens.
2.  **Emulsify:** Whisk in the tomato paste until smooth.
3.  **The Liquid:** Slowly pour in the broth while whisking vigorously to remove all lumps.
4.  **Simmer:** Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
5.  **Finish:** Remove from heat. Whisk in the vinegar and black pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.
6.  **Store:** Use immediately or store in a glass jar in the fridge for up to 1 week.

3 tbsp All-Purpose Flour (or GF blend)

1 tsp Ground Cumin

2 cups Vegetable or Chicken Broth

data.description: Overnight no-knead dough, tomato sauce and a mozzarella-Parmesan topping bar, baked as four personal pizzas.

scaling.reason: The dough makes four 10-inch pizzas or two 14-inch pizzas with matched topping portions. Use the complete batch and its specified geometry; baking and fermentation times do not scale arithmetically.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Combine {{ingredients}} until no dry flour remains. The dough will be sticky. Cover the bowl; no kneading is needed.

steps.title: Ferment overnight
steps.text: Let the covered dough rise around 72°F / 22°C until it is bubbly and more than doubled, approximately 18 hours. Check earlier in a warm room and allow longer in a cool one. When ready, portion it as below; do not extend the room-temperature rise blindly to two days.

For two 14-inch pizzas, divide into two approximately 434 g portions instead. Fold the edges underneath to make rounded balls without flattening out all the gas. steps.title: Set up the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 500°F. For the pan route, use two room-temperature metal pans rated for that temperature, with enough flat area for the chosen diameter, and bake one at a time on the middle rack. A 14-inch round requires a suitably large round pan; do not assume it fits a standard baking sheet. For the stone route, put a suitably rated stone in the cold oven and preheat it for 1 hour; the stone and peel must fit the chosen diameter. Neither route uses parchment. Keep used pans aside to cool before reloading.

steps.title: Cook the sauce batch
steps.text: Have {{ingredients}} ready. Warm the oil over medium-low heat, add the garlic and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant but not browned. Stir in the tomatoes, salt and optional pepper flakes. Simmer 10–15 minutes, stirring, until spreadable without a puddle of loose liquid; add the optional basil at the end. Let cool enough to handle. Measure 3/4 cup for the full pizza batch and refrigerate the surplus promptly; the whole can is not meant to go onto the pizzas. If using prepared sauce instead, omit this entire sauce component and measure 3/4 cup thick pizza sauce.

steps.title: Shape one pizza
steps.text: Use {{ingredients}} as needed. Stretch one ball to its chosen 10-inch or 14-inch diameter, leaving a thicker rim. Cover and wait another 10 minutes if it springs back. Move the untopped round onto a lightly oiled cool pan, or a lightly floured peel and confirm it slides. Keep unused dough covered and prepared perishable toppings chilled.

steps.title: Allocate cheese and toppings
steps.text: Divide {{ingredients}} into four sets for small pizzas or two sets for large ones. Each 10-inch pizza gets 3 tbsp prepared sauce, 3 oz mozzarella and 1/4 oz Parmesan; each 14-inch pizza gets 6 tbsp sauce, 6 oz mozzarella and 1/2 oz Parmesan. Spread its sauce leaving a 1/2- to 3/4-inch rim. Add half of that pizza’s mozzarella, a sparse layer of the chosen toppings, then its remaining mozzarella and its full Parmesan portion. On a peel, check again that it slides and bake immediately. Use ready-to-eat pepperoni or fully cooked sausage, bacon or chicken; thinly slice quick-cooking vegetables, cook and cool mushrooms first, and drain wet toppings. Keep perishable toppings chilled until assembly.

steps.title: Bake one at a time
steps.text: Put the pan on the middle rack, or launch directly onto the stone. Start checking at 10 minutes; roughly 12–15 minutes is a guide, not a fixed endpoint for every size, cheese and baking surface. The underside should be browned, the center set and the rim golden, with melted cheese. Rotate safely with the pan or peel if browning is uneven, and allow longer if the bottom is pale. Keep the oven on between pizzas and give a stone about 5 minutes to recover.

steps.title: Finish and serve in rounds
steps.text: Add {{ingredients}} after baking. Rest the pizza on a rack for 2–3 minutes, cut and serve. Shape, top and bake each remaining pizza separately, using its assigned sauce and cheese. Alternate pans and let them cool before reloading; never assemble on a hot pan. Four pizzas mean four oven rounds, not one 15-minute bake.

learning.focus: Match weighed dough, fermentation and pizza size
learning.outcome: An airy, stretchable dough baked into a browned base with melted cheese and evenly distributed toppings.
before: Weigh the dough ingredients. This is a 70% hydration dough; adding water by an unrelated cup conversion changes its handling.
Choose four 10-inch pizzas or two 14-inch pizzas before portioning; check the pan or stone fits. The total cheese and sauce used remain the same.

Optional toppings: ready-to-eat pepperoni, thin red onion or bell pepper, cooked and cooled mushrooms, prepared caramelized onions, fully cooked sausage or bacon, cooked chicken, roasted garlic, dry spinach, drained artichokes or a few blotted tomato slices. Choose a sparse layer rather than every option. Preparing these is additional unless already done.

checkpoints.cue: Dough is aerated and more than doubled, rather than simply old enough.
checkpoints.why: Room temperature changes fermentation speed; the clock alone does not establish readiness.

checkpoints.cue: Each pizza has its own measured cheese and sauce set, with no pile of wet toppings.
checkpoints.why: Dividing first prevents using the entire batch’s cheese on the first pizza and controls moisture.

checkpoints.cue: The center is set and the underside browned.
checkpoints.why: A golden rim can develop before the wetter center has finished baking.

troubleshooting.cause: It is cold, tight from shaping or has not relaxed enough.
troubleshooting.fix: Cover and wait another 10 minutes. Do not tear it wider or force in handfuls of flour; refrigerated portions may need their full warming period.

troubleshooting.cause: Fresh mozzarella or toppings released excess water.
troubleshooting.fix: Finish baking to a set base, extending time as needed. Next time drain and blot the cheese and wet toppings, or choose the low-moisture cheese option.

substitutions.alternative: The same weight of whole-milk low-moisture mozzarella, grated
substitutions.effect: Less free moisture and a more even melt; browning and bake time may differ.

substitutions.alternative: 3/4 cup prepared thick pizza sauce for the whole batch
substitutions.effect: Omit the tomatoes, sauce oil, garlic, salt, flakes and sauce basil; there will be no extra sauce batch to save.

substitutions.alternative: Suitable cheeses made with vegetarian rennet, with no meat toppings
substitutions.effect: Makes a vegetarian option when all ingredients are suitable; saltiness and melting vary.

learning.timing: Allow about 21 hours on the unrefrigerated route: roughly 18 hours of bulk fermentation, an hour of relaxation overlapping oven heating and sauce preparation, then serial baking and serving. Four pizzas take roughly 48–60 minutes of baking plus handling and any stone recovery; two larger pizzas need two rounds. About 45 minutes is active work, excluding cooking optional toppings from scratch. The refrigerated route adds its chosen storage period and uses a 2–3-hour warm-up instead of the one-hour rest.
learning.storage: Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, in shallow covered containers at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F / 74°C throughout. Store the raw, fermented dough only by the separate three-day refrigeration instructions in step 3. Do not taste raw dough.

body:
## Chef's Note

An overnight rest develops a dough that stretches with little kneading, leaving most of the work for topping and baking. The weighed dough is adapted from Jim Lahey’s no-knead method, published by [J. Kenji López-Alt in Serious Eats](https://www.seriouseats.com/jim-laheys-no-knead-pizza-dough-recipe). This version makes four 10-inch pizzas or two 14-inch pizzas for four portions; divide the cheese and sauce first, then serve the pizzas as they finish.

## Directions

1. **Mix the dough:** Combine all-purpose flour, water, fine sea salt, and active-dry yeast until no dry flour remains. The dough will be sticky. Cover the bowl; no kneading is needed.
2. **Ferment overnight:** Let the covered dough rise around 72°F / 22°C until it is bubbly and more than doubled, approximately 18 hours. Check earlier in a warm room and allow longer in a cool one. When ready, portion it as below; do not extend the room-temperature rise blindly to two days.
3. **Portion and relax:** Lightly dust the work surface with flour. For four 10-inch pizzas, divide the dough into four equal portions, approximately 217 g each. For two 14-inch pizzas, divide into two approximately 434 g portions instead. Fold the edges underneath to make rounded balls without flattening out all the gas. Cover and rest about 1 hour until pliable. Alternatively, cover the risen, portioned dough individually and refrigerate up to 3 days; on baking day allow the covered balls about 2–3 hours at room temperature to relax instead of the one-hour rest. Prepare the oven and toppings during the last hour.
4. **Set up the oven:** Heat the oven to 500°F. For the pan route, use two room-temperature metal pans rated for that temperature, with enough flat area for the chosen diameter, and bake one at a time on the middle rack. A 14-inch round requires a suitably large round pan; do not assume it fits a standard baking sheet. For the stone route, put a suitably rated stone in the cold oven and preheat it for 1 hour; the stone and peel must fit the chosen diameter. Neither route uses parchment. Keep used pans aside to cool before reloading.
5. **Cook the sauce batch:** Have whole peeled tomatoes, olive oil, garlic cloves, fine salt, red pepper flakes (if using), and fresh basil (if using) ready. Warm the oil over medium-low heat, add the garlic and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant but not browned. Stir in the tomatoes, salt and optional pepper flakes. Simmer 10–15 minutes, stirring, until spreadable without a puddle of loose liquid; add the optional basil at the end. Let cool enough to handle. Measure 3/4 cup for the full pizza batch and refrigerate the surplus promptly; the whole can is not meant to go onto the pizzas. If using prepared sauce instead, omit this entire sauce component and measure 3/4 cup thick pizza sauce.
6. **Shape one pizza:** Use flour and olive oil (if using) as needed. Stretch one ball to its chosen 10-inch or 14-inch diameter, leaving a thicker rim. Cover and wait another 10 minutes if it springs back. Move the untopped round onto a lightly oiled cool pan, or a lightly floured peel and confirm it slides. Keep unused dough covered and prepared perishable toppings chilled.
7. **Allocate cheese and toppings:** Divide fresh mozzarella, Parmesan, and prepared pizza toppings (if using) into four sets for small pizzas or two sets for large ones. Each 10-inch pizza gets 3 tbsp prepared sauce, 3 oz mozzarella and 1/4 oz Parmesan; each 14-inch pizza gets 6 tbsp sauce, 6 oz mozzarella and 1/2 oz Parmesan. Spread its sauce leaving a 1/2- to 3/4-inch rim. Add half of that pizza’s mozzarella, a sparse layer of the chosen toppings, then its remaining mozzarella and its full Parmesan portion. On a peel, check again that it slides and bake immediately. Use ready-to-eat pepperoni or fully cooked sausage, bacon or chicken; thinly slice quick-cooking vegetables, cook and cool mushrooms first, and drain wet toppings. Keep perishable toppings chilled until assembly.
8. **Bake one at a time:** Put the pan on the middle rack, or launch directly onto the stone. Start checking at 10 minutes; roughly 12–15 minutes is a guide, not a fixed endpoint for every size, cheese and baking surface. The underside should be browned, the center set and the rim golden, with melted cheese. Rotate safely with the pan or peel if browning is uneven, and allow longer if the bottom is pale. Keep the oven on between pizzas and give a stone about 5 minutes to recover.
9. **Finish and serve in rounds:** Add fresh basil (if using) after baking. Rest the pizza on a rack for 2–3 minutes, cut and serve. Shape, top and bake each remaining pizza separately, using its assigned sauce and cheese. Alternate pans and let them cool before reloading; never assemble on a hot pan. Four pizzas mean four oven rounds, not one 15-minute bake.

## Toppings and shortcuts

Choose a sparse layer of ready-to-eat pepperoni, thin red onion or bell pepper, cooked and cooled mushrooms, prepared caramelized onions, fully cooked sausage or bacon, cooked chicken, roasted garlic, dry spinach, drained artichokes or a few blotted tomato slices. Optional toppings are additional to the measured cheese; they are not all required. Keep perishable toppings refrigerated until assembly. Fresh basil goes on after baking.

The same weight of whole-milk low-moisture mozzarella can replace fresh mozzarella; it releases less free moisture and browns differently. For prepared sauce, omit the whole sauce-making component and use 3/4 cup thick pizza sauce for all the pizzas. For a vegetarian version, choose suitable cheeses made with vegetarian rennet and omit meat toppings.

## Timing and leftovers

Plan about 21 hours for the overnight route, mostly hands-off. Sauce preparation and oven heating overlap the one-hour dough rest; four separate bakes take roughly 48–60 minutes plus handling and any stone recovery. Preparing optional toppings from scratch adds work. The refrigerated dough route uses the separate 2–3-hour warm-up in step 3. Do not taste raw dough.

Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F / 74°C throughout. Cool and refrigerate surplus sauce promptly in a shallow container. Raw dough follows the separate three-day refrigeration limit in step 3.

export.notes:
Chef's Note

An overnight rest develops a dough that stretches with little kneading, leaving most of the work for topping and baking. The weighed dough is adapted from Jim Lahey’s no-knead method, published by J. Kenji López-Alt in Serious Eats (https://www.seriouseats.com/jim-laheys-no-knead-pizza-dough-recipe). This version makes four 10-inch pizzas or two 14-inch pizzas for four portions; divide the cheese and sauce first, then serve the pizzas as they finish.

Toppings and shortcuts

Choose a sparse layer of ready-to-eat pepperoni, thin red onion or bell pepper, cooked and cooled mushrooms, prepared caramelized onions, fully cooked sausage or bacon, cooked chicken, roasted garlic, dry spinach, drained artichokes or a few blotted tomato slices. Optional toppings are additional to the measured cheese; they are not all required. Keep perishable toppings refrigerated until assembly. Fresh basil goes on after baking.

The same weight of whole-milk low-moisture mozzarella can replace fresh mozzarella; it releases less free moisture and browns differently. For prepared sauce, omit the whole sauce-making component and use 3/4 cup thick pizza sauce for all the pizzas. For a vegetarian version, choose suitable cheeses made with vegetarian rennet and omit meat toppings.

Timing and leftovers

Plan about 21 hours for the overnight route, mostly hands-off. Sauce preparation and oven heating overlap the one-hour dough rest; four separate bakes take roughly 48–60 minutes plus handling and any stone recovery. Preparing optional toppings from scratch adds work. The refrigerated dough route uses the separate 2–3-hour warm-up in step 3. Do not taste raw dough.

Refrigerate perishable leftovers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days or freeze; reheat to 165°F / 74°C throughout. Cool and refrigerate surplus sauce promptly in a shallow container. Raw dough follows the separate three-day refrigeration limit in step 3.

Source: Dough adapted from Jim Lahey, published by J. Kenji López-Alt in Serious Eats

data.title: Rice & Orzo Pilaf
ingredients: 1 cup (200 g) long-grain white rice, not parboiled or instant
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, optional finish
2 tbsp hot water, only if needed to finish firm grains
data.description: Long-grain rice and golden toasted orzo cooked in broth, then rested before fluffing. Optional lemon is added at the end.

learning.focus: Toast for flavor, then hydrate and rest
learning.outcome: Tender rice and distinct golden orzo, with no hard core or pool of broth.
before: Use a 2–3 quart saucepan with a tight lid. A wide pan or leaky lid loses more water.
The method is for ordinary long-grain white rice and standard orzo. Parboiled rice, brown rice, and very large pasta shapes do not share its timing.

checkpoints.cue: Orzo is golden brown, not dark mahogany.
checkpoints.why: Toasting adds flavor, but burned pasta stays bitter after liquid is added.

checkpoints.cue: Liquid is absorbed and a tasted grain is nearly tender.
checkpoints.why: Absorption alone can also mean water escaped too quickly; tasting distinguishes hydrated rice from a dry pan with hard grains.

checkpoints.cue: After the covered rest, rice fluffs without a wet bottom.
checkpoints.why: The rest lets remaining moisture redistribute and finish hydration without continued direct heat.

troubleshooting.problem: Rice is firm and pan is dry
troubleshooting.cause: Excess evaporation or a rice brand that needs more water.
troubleshooting.fix: Sprinkle in the measured 2 tbsp hot water, cover, cook gently another 3–5 minutes, and rest again. Add a little more only if still needed.

troubleshooting.cause: The pan retained more water or the rice needs a little longer.
troubleshooting.fix: If grains are still firm, keep simmering briefly. If tender, leave uncovered on very low heat for a minute or two, then rest off heat.

substitutions.alternative: Unsalted vegetable broth
substitutions.effect: Makes the pilaf vegetarian with a somewhat different flavor. Salt to taste if using a seasoned broth.

learning.timing: 40 minutes includes five minutes preparation, about 25 minutes cooking including toasting and heating broth, and a ten-minute covered rest.
learning.storage: Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C), at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days; reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Spread into shallow containers promptly; do not cool it slowly in the covered cooking pot.

body:
## Chef's Note

Toasted orzo gives this pilaf a nutty aroma and a texture slightly different from the rice. The rice and pasta share the broth, so the liquid has to hydrate both. A tight lid controls evaporation; tasting and a covered rest are more useful than treating one cooking time as universal.

## Directions

1. **Rinse rice:** Rinse the rice in several changes of cool water, then drain thoroughly in a fine-mesh strainer. Measure the other ingredients.
2. **Toast orzo:** Melt butter in a 2–3 quart saucepan over medium heat. Add dry orzo and stir frequently for 3–4 minutes until golden brown. Add drained rice and stir for 1 minute.
3. **Add seasonings and broth:** Stir in garlic powder, onion powder, optional turmeric, salt, and pepper for about 15 seconds. Pour in broth carefully and bring to a gentle boil.
4. **Simmer:** Stir once, cover tightly, and reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook about 15–18 minutes. Check that the liquid is absorbed and taste a grain. If it remains hard and dry, add the measured hot water and cook covered a little longer.
5. **Rest and finish:** Once grains are nearly tender, turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently and fold in dried parsley and optional lemon juice. Taste before adding any further seasoning.

data.title: Ketchup
ingredients: 14 oz (400g) Tomato Passata or Crushed Tomatoes
3 tbsp Red Wine Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)
Salt and Black Pepper to taste

body:
## Chef's Note

Simmering tomato passata on lowest heat for 30 minutes slowly evaporates water and concentrates tomatoes' natural fructose, creating thick ketchup without added sugar. Red wine vinegar provides acidity that keeps the savory spices from tasting flat.

## Directions

1.  **Combine:** In a small non-reactive saucepan, whisk together the tomatoes, vinegar, smashed garlic, mustard, and all spices.
2.  **Reduce:** Bring to a tiny simmer over low heat. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent the bottom from scorching.
3.  **Refine:** Once thickened and dark red, remove the garlic clove.
4.  **Emulsion:** For the Kitchen Standard texture, use an immersion blender to puree the mixture until perfectly smooth and glossy.
5.  **Set:** Let cool completely. Transfer to an airtight glass jar and refrigerate.
6.  **Store:** Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
